wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.rootCharacteristics: FAO-56 lists a maximum effective rooting depth of 1.5–1.8 m for winter wheat in suitable soils.
limitations: Calendar assumes autumn-sown bread wheat in Central Anatolia. Active growth months are a model approximation.
Temperature and pH are broad EcoCrop reference bands. The FAO water range is a generic seasonal crop-water estimate. Rainfed crops can use less water and produce different yields.

barley.name: Barley
barley.rootCharacteristics: FAO-56 lists a maximum effective rooting depth of 1.0–1.5 m in suitable soils.
limitations: Calendar assumes autumn-sown barley in Central Anatolia. The active growth window and relative irrigation sensitivity are model assumptions.
Temperature and pH are broad EcoCrop reference bands. FAO groups barley, oats and wheat in its generic seasonal crop-water range.

chickpea.name: Chickpea
chickpea.rootCharacteristics: FAO-56 lists a maximum effective rooting depth of 0.6–1.0 m in suitable soils.
limitations: Calendar approximates spring sowing and summer harvest in Central Anatolia. Active growth months are a model approximation.

Temperature and pH use broad EcoCrop reference bands. The provisional rounded water band reflects supplemental to fuller irrigation treatments in a two-year Konya experiment. Rainfed treatments used less water.

lentil.name: Lentil
lentil.rootCharacteristics: FAO-56 lists a maximum effective rooting depth of 0.6–0.8 m in suitable soils.
limitations: Calendar represents a spring-sown green lentil scenario in Central Anatolia. Late-February planting assumes suitable field conditions and July is a conservative harvest cutoff. Winter cultivars have different windows.

Temperature and pH are broad EcoCrop reference bands. The provisional water band is informed by reported seasonal use in northern Syrian field experiments. Applicability to spring-sown lentil near Konya is unverified.

sunflower.name: Sunflower
sunflower.rootCharacteristics: FAO-56 lists a maximum effective rooting depth of 0.8–1.5 m in suitable soils.
limitations: Calendar represents main-season oilseed sunflower near Konya. The narrower planting window reflects local frost risk. Active growth months are a model approximation.
Temperature and pH are broad EcoCrop reference bands. The provisional seasonal water-use band comes from one Konya irrigation experiment and varies with climate and management.

maize.name: Maize
maize.rootCharacteristics: FAO-56 lists a maximum effective rooting depth of 1.0–1.7 m for grain maize in suitable soils.
limitations: Calendar represents main-season grain maize in Central Anatolia and uses a conservative October harvest cutoff. Cultivar maturity and local frost dates can shift the window.
Temperature and pH use broad FAO reference bands. The water range is for approximate seasonal crop water use under well-watered conditions. Flowering is particularly sensitive to water stress.
